claim: Phosphorylation at serine 10 of histone H3 (H3 S10) contributes to mitotic chromosome condensation.
source: Here, we report on how phosphorylation at serine 10 of histone H3 (H3 S10) contributes to this process.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data throughout showing effects of H3 S10 mutations on chromosome condensation.

claim: Chromosome condensation entails two temporally and mechanistically distinct processes.
source: Using a fluorescence-based assay to study local compaction of the chromatin fiber in living yeast cells, we show that chromosome condensation entails two temporally and mechanistically distinct processes.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing different timing and mechanisms for compaction and contraction.

claim: Nucleosome-nucleosome interaction triggered by H3 S10 phosphorylation and deacetylation of histone H4 promote short-range compaction of chromatin during early anaphase.
source: Initially, nucleosome-nucleosome interaction triggered by H3 S10 phosphorylation and deacetylation of histone H4 promote short-range compaction of chromatin during early anaphase.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing effects of H3 S10 phosphorylation and H4 deacetylation on chromatin compaction timing.

claim: Condensin mediates the axial contraction of chromosome arms, a process peaking later in anaphase.
source: Independently, condensin mediates the axial contraction of chromosome arms, a process peaking later in anaphase.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing condensin's role in axial contraction and its timing.

claim: Defects in chromatin compaction have no observable effect on axial contraction.
source: Whereas defects in chromatin compaction have no observable effect on axial contraction and condensin inactivation does not affect short-range chromatin compaction, inactivation of both pathways causes synergistic defects in chromosome segregation and cell viability.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing that H3 S10A and H4 mutations do not affect axial contraction.

claim: Condensin inactivation does not affect short-range chromatin compaction.
source: Whereas defects in chromatin compaction have no observable effect on axial contraction and condensin inactivation does not affect short-range chromatin compaction, inactivation of both pathways causes synergistic defects in chromosome segregation and cell viability.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing that smc2-8 mutation does not affect chromatin compaction.

claim: Inactivation of both chromatin compaction and axial contraction pathways causes synergistic defects in chromosome segregation and cell viability.
source: Whereas defects in chromatin compaction have no observable effect on axial contraction and condensin inactivation does not affect short-range chromatin compaction, inactivation of both pathways causes synergistic defects in chromosome segregation and cell viability.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing increased lagging chromatin and reduced viability in double mutants.

claim: Both chromatin compaction and axial contraction pathways rely at least partially on the deacetylase Hst2.
source: Furthermore, both pathways rely at least partially on the deacetylase Hst2, suggesting that this protein helps coordinating chromatin compaction and axial contraction to properly shape mitotic chromosomes.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing effects of hst2Δ on both compaction and contraction.

claim: Hst2 helps coordinate chromatin compaction and axial contraction to properly shape mitotic chromosomes.
source: Furthermore, both pathways rely at least partially on the deacetylase Hst2, suggesting that this protein helps coordinating chromatin compaction and axial contraction to properly shape mitotic chromosomes.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the observation that Hst2 affects both pathways.

claim: The DNA molecule at the core of any eukaryotic chromosome is a hundred to million times longer than the average diameter of the cell that hosts it.
source: The DNA molecule at the core of any eukaryotic chromosome is a hundred to million times longer than the average diameter of the cell that hosts it.
evidence: This is established knowledge about chromosome and cell dimensions.

claim: Cells need to fold their genetic material in order to fit it in the interphase nucleus.
source: Thus, cells need to fold their genetic material in order to fit it in the interphase nucleus; they need to pack it further during mitosis, in order to move sister-chromatids safely and symmetrically apart.
evidence: This is established knowledge about chromosome organization.

claim: Cells need to pack genetic material further during mitosis to move sister-chromatids safely and symmetrically apart.
source: Thus, cells need to fold their genetic material in order to fit it in the interphase nucleus; they need to pack it further during mitosis, in order to move sister-chromatids safely and symmetrically apart.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mitotic chromosome function.

claim: Chromatin folding must be dynamic to allow transcription and replication during interphase.
source: Furthermore, chromatin folding must be dynamic to allow transcription and replication during interphase, and such that exceptionally large chromosomes can hyper-condense during anaphase in order to fit the size of the spindle and prevent chromosome missegregation (Neurohr et al., 2011; Titos et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Exceptionally large chromosomes can hyper-condense during anaphase in order to fit the size of the spindle and prevent chromosome missegregation.
source: Furthermore, chromatin folding must be dynamic to allow transcription and replication during interphase, and such that exceptionally large chromosomes can hyper-condense during anaphase in order to fit the size of the spindle and prevent chromosome missegregation (Neurohr et al., 2011; Titos et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Mitotic condensation facilitates the decatenation of sister chromatids during their separation.
source: Moreover, mitotic condensation also facilitates the decatenation of sister chromatids during their separation (Charbin et al., 2014), and might help to 'cleanse' chromosomes from transcription, replication and cohesion factors (Yanagida, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Mitotic condensation might help to 'cleanse' chromosomes from transcription, replication and cohesion factors.
source: Moreover, mitotic condensation also facilitates the decatenation of sister chromatids during their separation (Charbin et al., 2014), and might help to 'cleanse' chromosomes from transcription, replication and cohesion factors (Yanagida, 2009).
evidence: This is a speculative idea supported by a citation.

claim: Chromosome cleansing might 'reset' the transcriptional state of genes.
source: This is thought to 'reset' the transcriptional state of genes, and prevent displaced factors from interfering with chromosome segregation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the cleansing hypothesis.

claim: Chromosome cleansing might prevent displaced factors from interfering with chromosome segregation.
source: This is thought to 'reset' the transcriptional state of genes, and prevent displaced factors from interfering with chromosome segregation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the cleansing hypothesis.

claim: The events ensuring the mitotic condensation of chromosomes are still only partially understood.
source: However, despite their importance for chromosome segregation, the events ensuring the mitotic condensation of chromosomes are still only partially understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Nucleosomes play a critical role in DNA packaging.
source: Early studies made evident that nucleosomes play a critical role in DNA packaging.
evidence: This is established knowledge from early studies.

claim: Histone H3 is phosphorylated by aurora B throughout mitosis on a serine at position 10 in most, if not all, eukaryotes.
source: In favor of the idea that they play specific roles in chromatin condensation, histone H3 is phosphorylated by aurora B throughout mitosis on a serine at position 10 in most, if not all, eukaryotes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about H3 phosphorylation.

claim: Aurora B inactivation leads to chromosome condensation and segregation defects in budding yeast.
source: Furthermore, aurora B inactivation leads to chromosome condensation and segregation defects in budding yeast (Lavoie et al., 2004), fission yeast (Petrova et al., 2013; Tada et al., 2011), HeLa cells (Tada et al., 2011) and roundworms (Hagstrom et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Aurora B inactivation leads to chromosome condensation and segregation defects in fission yeast.
source: Furthermore, aurora B inactivation leads to chromosome condensation and segregation defects in budding yeast (Lavoie et al., 2004), fission yeast (Petrova et al., 2013; Tada et al., 2011), HeLa cells (Tada et al., 2011) and roundworms (Hagstrom et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Aurora B inactivation leads to chromosome condensation and segregation defects in HeLa cells.
source: Furthermore, aurora B inactivation leads to chromosome condensation and segregation defects in budding yeast (Lavoie et al., 2004), fission yeast (Petrova et al., 2013; Tada et al., 2011), HeLa cells (Tada et al., 2011) and roundworms (Hagstrom et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Aurora B inactivation leads to chromosome condensation and segregation defects in roundworms.
source: Furthermore, aurora B inactivation leads to chromosome condensation and segregation defects in budding yeast (Lavoie et al., 2004), fission yeast (Petrova et al., 2013; Tada et al., 2011), HeLa cells (Tada et al., 2011) and roundworms (Hagstrom et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The precise role of H3 S10 phosphorylation has remained unclear.
source: However, the precise role of H3 S10 phosphorylation has remained unclear (Ajiro and Nishimoto, 1985).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: H3 S10 phosphorylation promotes the recruitment of the sirtuin-related deacetylase Hst2.
source: Recent data demonstrated that H3 S10 phosphorylation promotes the recruitment of the sirtuin-related deacetylase Hst2, which in turn deacetylates, at least, lysine 16 of histone H4 (Wilkins et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Hst2 deacetylates, at least, lysine 16 of histone H4.
source: Recent data demonstrated that H3 S10 phosphorylation promotes the recruitment of the sirtuin-related deacetylase Hst2, which in turn deacetylates, at least, lysine 16 of histone H4 (Wilkins et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Deacetylation of H4 K16 unmasks a basic patch, allowing H4 to interact with the acidic patch on H2A, most probably on an adjacent nucleosome.
source: This unmasks a basic patch, allowing H4 to interact with the acidic patch on H2A, most probably on an adjacent nucleosome (Robinson et al., 2008; Gordon et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The cascade of events initiated by H3 phosphorylation is thought to tighten the interaction between neighboring nucleosomes.
source: Thus, this cascade of events initiated by H3 phosphorylation is thought to tighten the interaction between neighboring nucleosomes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the H3-Hst2-H4-H2A pathway.

claim: All studies carried out so far have failed to reveal strong phenotypes for H3 serine 10 to alanine mutations in a plethora of model organisms.
source: However, all studies carried out so far have failed to reveal strong phenotypes for H3 serine 10 to alanine mutations in a plethora of model organisms (de la Barre et al., 2001; Afonso et al., 2014; Ditchfield et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Mutation of H3 S10 in budding yeast did not affect axial contraction of chromosomes during regular mitoses.
source: Furthermore, mutation of this residue in budding yeast did not affect axial contraction of chromosomes and the condensation of the rDNA during regular mitoses (Neurohr et al., 2011; Lavoie et al., 2004; Lavoie et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Mutation of H3 S10 in budding yeast did not affect the condensation of the rDNA during regular mitoses.
source: Furthermore, mutation of this residue in budding yeast did not affect axial contraction of chromosomes and the condensation of the rDNA during regular mitoses (Neurohr et al., 2011; Lavoie et al., 2004; Lavoie et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The only phenotype identified upon replacement of H3 S10 with alanine in yeast so far is limited to the reduced ability to hyper-condense artificially long chromosomes in order to fit them in the spindle.
source: Indeed, the only phenotype identified upon replacement of H3 S10 with alanine in yeast so far is limited to the reduced ability to hyper-condense artificially long chromosomes in order to fit them in the spindle (Neurohr et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: It remains unclear whether H3 phosphorylation and H4 deacetylation play any general role in mitotic chromosome condensation.
source: Thus, it remains unclear whether H3 phosphorylation and H4 deacetylation play any general role in mitotic chromosome condensation.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Mitotic extracts of frog eggs lacking any one of the subunits of condensin largely failed to condense chromosomes.
source: The discovery that mitotic extracts of frog eggs lacking any one of the subunits of a protein complex called condensin largely failed to condense chromosomes (Hirano and Mitchison, 1994) opened new perspectives for understanding chromosome condensation (Piazza et al., 2013; Thadani et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Condensin is a ring-shaped pentameric protein complex.
source: Condensin is a ring-shaped pentameric protein complex.
evidence: This is established knowledge about condensin structure.

claim: The core of the condensin ring is formed by two structural maintenance of chromosome (SMC) subunits, Smc2 and Smc4.
source: The core of the ring is formed by two structural maintenance of chromosome (SMC) subunits, Smc2 and Smc4.
evidence: This is established knowledge about condensin structure.

claim: Three non-SMC proteins (Brn1, Ycg1 and Ycs4 in budding yeast) close the condensin ring.
source: Three non-SMC proteins (Brn1, Ycg1 and Ycs4 in budding yeast) close the ring.
evidence: This is established knowledge about condensin structure.

claim: The mechanism of condensin loading on chromatin is not understood.
source: The mechanism of condensin loading on chromatin is not understood, but seems to depend on the activity of the kinase aurora B (Lavoie et al., 2004; Tada et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Condensin loading on chromatin seems to depend on the activity of the kinase aurora B.
source: The mechanism of condensin loading on chromatin is not understood, but seems to depend on the activity of the kinase aurora B (Lavoie et al., 2004; Tada et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The non-SMC subunits of condensin directly bind DNA.
source: Furthermore, the non-SMC subunits were recently shown to directly bind DNA (Piazza et al., 2014), potentially followed by topological entrapment of chromatin inside the condensin ring (Cuylen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: DNA binding by non-SMC subunits is potentially followed by topological entrapment of chromatin inside the condensin ring.
source: Furthermore, the non-SMC subunits were recently shown to directly bind DNA (Piazza et al., 2014), potentially followed by topological entrapment of chromatin inside the condensin ring (Cuylen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a speculative idea supported by a citation.

claim: How condensin performs its functions in chromosome condensation is unclear.
source: How condensin performs its functions in chromosome condensation is unclear, but it has been proposed that condensin's role might be structural, by inducing loops within the same DNA strand (Cuylen et al., 2011; Cuylen and Haering, 2011) or might be enzymatic by promoting positive DNA supercoiling (Baxter and Aragón, 2012), both assisting in a decrease in length of mitotic chromatids.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Condensin's role might be structural, by inducing loops within the same DNA strand.
source: How condensin performs its functions in chromosome condensation is unclear, but it has been proposed that condensin's role might be structural, by inducing loops within the same DNA strand (Cuylen et al., 2011; Cuylen and Haering, 2011) or might be enzymatic by promoting positive DNA supercoiling (Baxter and Aragón, 2012), both assisting in a decrease in length of mitotic chromatids.
evidence: This is a speculative idea supported by citations.

claim: Condensin's role might be enzymatic by promoting positive DNA supercoiling.
source: How condensin performs its functions in chromosome condensation is unclear, but it has been proposed that condensin's role might be structural, by inducing loops within the same DNA strand (Cuylen et al., 2011; Cuylen and Haering, 2011) or might be enzymatic by promoting positive DNA supercoiling (Baxter and Aragón, 2012), both assisting in a decrease in length of mitotic chromatids.
evidence: This is a speculative idea supported by a citation.

claim: Chromosomes can still, at least partially, condense in the absence of condensin in fission yeast, fly, chicken and mammalian cells.
source: Mitigating the central role of condensin in chromosome condensation, however, were observations in model organisms as diverse as fission yeast, fly, chicken and mammalian cells that indicate that chromosomes can still, at least partially, condense in the absence of condensin (Petrova et al., 2013; Coelho et al., 2003; Vagnarelli et al., 2006; Gerlich et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Condensin cannot be the sole factor shaping mitotic chromosomes.
source: Thus, although condensin was established as a key player in chromosome condensation, it cannot be the sole factor shaping mitotic chromosomes.
evidence: This is an inference based on observations that chromosomes can partially condense without condensin.

claim: There is a highly significant (p<0.0001), 2–2.5-fold decrease in mCherry fluorescence intensity at the TetO repeats on the anaphase compared with the G1-phase chromosomes.
source: After subtracting background fluorescence, we noticed a highly significant (p<0.0001), 2–2.5-fold decrease in mCherry fluorescence intensity at the TetO repeats on the anaphase compared with the G1-phase chromosomes (Figure 1A, B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A, B.

claim: Mutations that abrogate the mitotic interaction between H2A and H4, such as H3 S10A, hst2∆ and the H4 ∆9–16 mutations, all abolished the reduction in brightness of the TetR-mCherry focus normally observed in anaphase cells.
source: Strikingly, mutations that abrogate the mitotic interaction between H2A and H4, such as H3 S10A, hst2∆ and the H4 ∆9–16 mutations, all abolished the reduction in brightness of the TetR-mCherry focus normally observed in anaphase cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Mutations that promote constitutive H2A/H4 interaction, such as H3 S10D and H4 K16R, caused the TetR-mCherry focus to constitutively show the low fluorescence intensity normally specific of anaphase cells.
source: In reverse, mutations that promote constitutive H2A/H4 interaction, such as H3 S10D and H4 K16R, caused the TetR-mCherry focus to constitutively show, that is, even in G1 cells, the low fluorescence intensity normally specific of anaphase cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The effect of the H3 S10D mutation was mediated by the recruitment of Hst2, since the hst2Δ mutation suppressed it.
source: The effect of the H3 S10D mutation was indeed mediated by the recruitment of Hst2, since the hst2Δ mutation suppressed it; the H3 S10D hst2∆ double mutant cells showed constitutive high brightness, similar to hst2∆ single mutant cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing genetic suppression.

claim: H4 K16 is not the sole residue that Hst2 deacetylates to promote nucleosome-nucleosome interaction.
source: Interestingly, however, introducing the H4 K16R mutation in the hst2∆ mutant cells did not restore the intensity drop normally observed during anaphase, suggesting that H4 K16 is not the sole residue that Hst2 deacetylates to promote nucleosome-nucleosome interaction (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data showing that H4 K16R does not suppress hst2Δ.

claim: A similar, and significant, decrease in reporter brightness in anaphase compared with G1 cells is observed at the LYS4 locus.
source: Although the effect was slightly less pronounced, we observed a similar, and significant, decrease in reporter brightness in anaphase compared with G1 cells at this locus (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Mutants in the H3 S10 pathway also affected fluctuations in intensity at the CEN distal locus.
source: As for the TRP1 locus, mutants in the H3 S10 pathway also affected fluctuations in intensity at the CEN distal locus: hst2∆, H3 S10A and H3S10D hst2∆ showed a continuously higher fluorescent intensity on the LacO repeats near the LYS4 gene and the H3 S10D mutation also resulted in a continuously lower fluorescent signal.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data at the LYS4 locus.

claim: Changes in chromatin organization during mitosis affected either the recruitment or the fluorescence intensity of TetR-mCherry and LacI-GFP on two distant chromatin loci.
source: These data indicated that changes in chromatin organization during mitosis indeed affected either the recruitment or the fluorescence intensity of TetR-mCherry and LacI-GFP on two distant chromatin loci, one close to the centromere and the second in the middle of the second longest yeast chromosome arm.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from two loci.

claim: Ipl1 activity is required for the intensity decrease of TetR-mCherry at the TRP1 locus in mitotic cells.
source: Since chromatin condensation is regulated by the kinase aurora B (Ipl1 in budding yeast), we last asked whether Ipl1 activity is required for the intensity decrease of TetR-mCherry at the TRP1 locus in mitotic cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that ipl1-321 cells fail to show intensity decrease at restrictive temperature.

claim: The ipl1-321 strain showed a significantly brighter dot when undergoing anaphase at the restrictive temperature.
source: Whereas wild type cells showed no significant difference in G1 and anaphase TetO/TetR-mCherry fluorescence intensity, the ipl1-321 strain showed a significantly brighter dot when undergoing anaphase at the restrictive temperature.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The enhanced H2A-H4 interaction triggered by aurora B-dependent recruitment of the deacetylase Hst2 onto chromatin affects the intensity of the TetR-mCherry signal on the chromosome.
source: Thus, we conclude that the enhanced H2A-H4 interaction triggered by aurora B-dependent recruitment of the deacetylase Hst2 onto chromatin indeed affects the intensity of the TetR-mCherry signal on the chromosome.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data from multiple mutants.

claim: Cells expressing both TetR-mCherry and TetR-GFP failed to show significant variation of the fluorescence signal for either mCherry or GFP at the TetO array between anaphase and G1.
source: Remarkably, unlike the cells expressing only TetR-mCherry, cells expressing both versions of TetR failed to show significant variation of the fluorescence signal for either mCherry or GFP at the TetO array between anaphase and G1 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: FRET was observed upon exciting in the GFP and recording emission in the red channel in cells expressing both TetR-mCherry and TetR-GFP, but not in cells expressing TetR-mCherry alone.
source: Supporting the idea that the intensity drop was due to a quenching effect, FRET was indeed observed upon exciting in the GFP and recording emission in the red channel in cells expressing both TetR-mCherry and TetR-GFP, but not in cells expressing TetR-mCherry alone (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: FRET was significantly increased during anaphase compared with G1-phase.
source: Moreover, FRET was significantly increased during anaphase compared with G1-phase (Figure 2B,C), indicating that the fluorophores are indeed brought in closer proximity during anaphase compared with interphase.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B,C.

claim: Increased H2A/H4 interaction results in a tighter packing of fluorophores and their quenching.
source: We conclude that increased H2A/H4 interaction results in a tighter packing of fluorophores and their quenching, establishing that H2A/H4 interaction leads to compaction of mitotic chromatin in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data showing quenching and FRET.

claim: H2A/H4 interaction leads to compaction of mitotic chromatin in vivo.
source: We conclude that increased H2A/H4 interaction results in a tighter packing of fluorophores and their quenching, establishing that H2A/H4 interaction leads to compaction of mitotic chromatin in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data showing quenching and FRET.

claim: Cell cycle dependent changes of TetR-mCherry or TetR-GFP signals on TetO arrays is a reliable measure of short-range compaction of the underlying chromatin.
source: Furthermore, cell cycle dependent changes of TetR-mCherry or TetR-GFP signals on TetO arrays is a reliable measure of short-range compaction of the underlying chromatin.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental validation of the assay.

claim: The intensity of the LacI-GFP signal was lowest during the first 12 minutes of anaphase.
source: Upon averaging the signal of at least 15 (t = -18 minutes) to maximum 31 (t = 0 minutes) such traces, we observed that the intensity of the signal was indeed lowest during the first 12 minutes of anaphase, while starting to increase as soon as the cells started to exit mitosis (Figure 3B, blue line indicates the formation of the first bud in the population).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Fluorescence intensity at the LacO locus was highly variable throughout every single movie, leading to high standard deviations.
source: We also noticed that fluorescence intensity at the LacO locus was highly variable throughout every single movie, leading to high standard deviations.
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data.

claim: Fluorescence variation was lowest during anaphase and started to increase as soon as chromatin was decondensing.
source: This variation was lowest during anaphase and started to increase as soon as chromatin was decondensing, consistent with the idea that chromatin is more constrained when it is most compacted and fluorophore quenching is highest.
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data with an interpretation.

claim: The quenching assay is statistical in nature.
source: In either case, this intrinsic cell-to-cell variability precludes drawing conclusions at the single cell level and emphasizes the fact that the quenching assay introduced here is statistical in nature.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observed variability in the data.

claim: During early anaphase, both the TetO and LacO array seemed to be compacted to some extent already.
source: Analysis of this data set indicated that the two marked loci underwent compaction and decompaction with slightly different kinetics (Figure 3C, upper panel). During early anaphase, both the TetO and LacO array seemed to be compacted to some extent already.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: As cells progressed to mid anaphase, the CEN4 proximal TetO arrays seemed slightly more compacted than the distal LacO arrays.
source: As cells progressed to mid anaphase, the CEN4 proximal TetO arrays seemed slightly more compacted than the distal LacO arrays.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In late anaphase, the TetO array was already starting to unpack, whereas the LacO remained compacted.
source: In late anaphase, the TetO array was already starting to unpack, whereas the LacO remained compacted.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Both TetO and LacO dots had recovered their full intensity in the G1 cells.
source: Both dots had recovered their full intensity in the G1 cells, demonstrating that the intensity decrease in anaphase was not solely the consequence of sister-chromatid separation, which is expected to reduce fluorescence intensity by half, down to its G1 level until the next S-phase.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The chromosome first stretched out upon anaphase onset, to subsequently contract, reaching their shortest length in late anaphase.
source: In the same cells, measuring the TetO-LacO distance (Figure 3C, lower panel) indicated that the chromosome first stretched out upon anaphase onset, to subsequently contract, reaching their shortest length in late anaphase, as reported (Guacci et al., 1994; Harrison et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and citations to previous work.

claim: The TetO-LacO distance re-extended to its steady state average in G1 cells.
source: The TetO-LacO distance re-extended then to its steady state average in G1 cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: No significant changes in nuclear diameter were observed when comparing late anaphase and the G1 phase in wild type and hst2Δ cells.
source: However, we did not observe any significant changes in nuclear diameter (as determined by GFP-tagging the nucleoporin Nup170) when comparing late anaphase and the G1 phase in wild type and hst2Δ cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The shortening of the TRP1-LYS4 distance in late anaphase cells truly reflects the effect of chromatin condensation by axial contraction of the chromosomes.
source: Thus, the shortening of the TRP1-LYS4 distance in late anaphase cells truly reflects the effect of chromatin condensation by axial contraction of the chromosomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that nuclear diameter does not change.

claim: Short-range chromatin compaction was not strictly concomitant with long-range axial contraction of the chromosome, but rather preceded it.
source: Furthermore, our results established that short-range chromatin compaction was not strictly concomitant with long-range axial contraction of the chromosome, but rather preceded it.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the kinetic data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Condensin inactivation for 90 min at the restrictive temperature had no effect on the changes in mCherry brightness between the anaphase and G1-phase of the cell cycle.
source: Remarkably, condensin inactivation for 90 min at the restrictive temperature had no effect on the changes in mCherry brightness between the anaphase and G1-phase of the cell cycle, whereas it indeed abrogated shortening of the TetO-LacO distance during anaphase (see below).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Condensin, unlike histone 3 phosphorylation and histone 4 deacetylation, does not promote nucleosome-nucleosome interaction.
source: We therefore conclude that condensin, unlike histone 3 phosphorylation and histone 4 deacetylation, does not promote nucleosome-nucleosome interaction.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data showing no effect of smc2-8 on chromatin compaction.

claim: H4/H2A crosslinking is observed in mitosis and correlated strongly with H4 K16 deacetylation in wild type cells.
source: In wild type cells, as reported before, H4/H2A crosslinking is observed in mitosis and correlated strongly with H4 K16 deacetylation (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The crosslinking between H4 and H2A showed no difference in kinetics in the condensin inactivated and in the wild type cells.
source: In fitting with the microscopy data (Figure 4A), the crosslinking between H4 and H2A showed no difference in kinetics in the condensin inactivated and in the wild type cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Condensin function is not required for proper, short-range compaction of mitotic chromatin.
source: Thus, condensin function is not required for proper, short-range compaction of mitotic chromatin.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data from microscopy and crosslinking assays.

claim: The ipl1-321 mutant cells failed to undergo chromosome contraction when shifted to the restrictive temperature prior to mitosis, compared with wild type cells at these temperatures.
source: Confirming the role of aurora B/Ipl1 in chromosome condensation, the ipl1-321 mutant cells failed to undergo chromosome contraction when shifted to the restrictive temperature prior to mitosis, compared with wild type cells at these temperatures (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The mutations H3 S10A and H4 Δ9–16 did not impair anaphase contraction.
source: As expected from previous studies (Neurohr et al., 2011; Lavoie et al., 2002), the function of Ipl1 in the contraction of regular chromosomes was unlikely to require H3 S10 phosphorylation and H2/H4 interaction, since the mutations H3 S10A and H4 Δ9–16 did not impair anaphase contraction (Figure 5B,C ).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B,C and citations to previous work.

claim: Ipl1 promotes the axial contraction of chromosomes independently of phosphorylating H3 S10 and of promoting H4/H2A interaction.
source: Thus, Ipl1 promotes the axial contraction of chromosomes independently of phosphorylating H3 S10 and of promoting H4/H2A interaction, but possibly by promoting condensin function (see discussion).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data showing no effect of H3 S10A on contraction.

claim: The hst2∆ mutation abrogated the proper contraction of the chromosome during mitosis.
source: In contrast, the hst2∆ mutation did abrogate the proper contraction of the chromosome during mitosis, implying that Hst2 acts in both axial chromosome contraction and short-range chromatin compaction (Figures 5C and 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5C and 1B.

claim: Hst2 acts in both axial chromosome contraction and short-range chromatin compaction.
source: In contrast, the hst2∆ mutation did abrogate the proper contraction of the chromosome during mitosis, implying that Hst2 acts in both axial chromosome contraction and short-range chromatin compaction (Figures 5C and 1B).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data showing effects of hst2Δ on both processes.

claim: The H3 S10D phospho-mimicking allele caused chromosome IV to remain in a constitutive state of axial contraction throughout the cell cycle.
source: Even more remarkably, the H3 S10D phospho-mimicking allele caused chromosome IV to remain in a constitutive state of axial contraction throughout the cell cycle (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: The constitutive contraction in H3 S10D cells most probably reflected constitutive recruitment of Hst2 to nucleosomes, since inactivation of the HST2 gene in these cells abolished contraction.
source: This most probably reflected constitutive recruitment of Hst2 to nucleosomes, since inactivation of the HST2 gene in these cells abolished contraction (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data showing genetic suppression.

claim: Boosting the recruitment of Hst2 to chromatin through mimicking constitutive and ubiquitous phosphorylation of H3 promoted both chromatin compaction and axial chromosome contraction.
source: Thus, boosting the recruitment of Hst2 to chromatin through mimicking constitutive and ubiquitous phosphorylation of H3 promoted both chromatin compaction and axial chromosome contraction, despite the fact that the H3-dependent pathway of Hst2 recruitment is normally dispensable for Hst2 function in axial chromosome contraction during regular mitoses (though, it is essential for adaptive hyper-condensation of an artificially long chromosome).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data from H3 S10D mutants.

claim: The H3-dependent pathway of Hst2 recruitment is normally dispensable for Hst2 function in axial chromosome contraction during regular mitoses.
source: Thus, boosting the recruitment of Hst2 to chromatin through mimicking constitutive and ubiquitous phosphorylation of H3 promoted both chromatin compaction and axial chromosome contraction, despite the fact that the H3-dependent pathway of Hst2 recruitment is normally dispensable for Hst2 function in axial chromosome contraction during regular mitoses (though, it is essential for adaptive hyper-condensation of an artificially long chromosome).
evidence: This is based on the observation that H3 S10A does not affect regular chromosome contraction.

claim: The H3-dependent pathway of Hst2 recruitment is essential for adaptive hyper-condensation of an artificially long chromosome.
source: Thus, boosting the recruitment of Hst2 to chromatin through mimicking constitutive and ubiquitous phosphorylation of H3 promoted both chromatin compaction and axial chromosome contraction, despite the fact that the H3-dependent pathway of Hst2 recruitment is normally dispensable for Hst2 function in axial chromosome contraction during regular mitoses (though, it is essential for adaptive hyper-condensation of an artificially long chromosome).
evidence: This is based on previous work cited earlier in the manuscript.

claim: The H4 K16R allele did not show any significant differences in chromosome contraction compared with wild type cells.
source: In accordance with the idea that H4 deacetylation solely plays a role in mitotic chromatin compaction, the H4 K16R allele did not show any significant differences in chromosome contraction compared with wild type cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: When HST2 was deleted on top of H4 K16R, a significant decrease in chromosome contraction was observed as compared with wild type and H4 K16R cells, but no significant difference with hst2∆ cells.
source: When we deleted HST2 on top of H4 K16R, we observed a significant decrease in chromosome contraction as compared with wild type and H4 K16R cells, but no significant difference with hst2∆ cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: H4 deacetylation has no evident role in chromosome contraction.
source: Based on this we conclude that H4 deacetylation has no evident role in chromosome contraction.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data from H4 K16R mutants.

claim: HST2, when deleted, does not have its defects on chromosome contraction through the chromatin compaction pathway, but rather by acting on another factor.
source: Furthermore, our data suggest that HST2, when deleted, does not have its defects on chromosome contraction through the chromatin compaction pathway, but rather by acting on another factor.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that H4 K16R does not suppress hst2Δ contraction defects.

claim: Axial contraction of chromosomes and compaction of chromatin are two independent processes.
source: Together, in agreement with the fact that they follow different kinetics (Figure 3), our data reveal that axial contraction of chromosomes and compaction of chromatin are two independent processes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data showing different kinetics and genetic requirements.

claim: Axial contraction and chromatin compaction depend on distinct molecular pathways that are at least in part coordinated by the same regulatory input, namely the activity of the kinase aurora B and the deacetylase Hst2.
source: They depend on distinct molecular pathways that are at least in part coordinated by the same regulatory input, namely the activity of the kinase aurora B and the deacetylase Hst2.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data showing roles of Ipl1 and Hst2 in both processes.

claim: Hst2 might not only promote chromosome compaction, but also the function of factors required for the axial contraction of chromatids, such as condensin.
source: Thus, we rationalized that Hst2 might not only promote chromosome compaction, but also the function of factors required for the axial contraction of chromatids, such as condensin.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on the observation that hst2Δ affects contraction.

claim: The smc2-8 single mutant cells grown at the restrictive temperature failed to axially contract their mitotic chromosomes to wild type levels.
source: As expected, the smc2-8 single mutant cells grown at the restrictive temperature failed to axially contract their mitotic chromosomes to wild type levels (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Deletion of Hst2 in smc2-8 cells did not exacerbate their contraction phenotype.
source: Deletion of Hst2 in these cells did not exacerbate their contraction phenotype (Figure 6A), suggesting that condensin and Hst2 might act in the same genetic pathway.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Condensin and Hst2 might act in the same genetic pathway.
source: Deletion of Hst2 in these cells did not exacerbate their contraction phenotype (Figure 6A), suggesting that condensin and Hst2 might act in the same genetic pathway.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the lack of additive phenotype.

claim: Contraction was restored in the H3 S10D smc2-8 double mutant cells.
source: In contrast, contraction was restored in the H3 S10D smc2-8 double mutant cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The restoration of contraction in H3 S10D smc2-8 cells was likely due to boosting Hst2 recruitment and activity since it disappeared in the H3 S10D hst2∆ smc2-8 triple mutant cells.
source: This effect was likely due to boosting Hst2 recruitment and activity since it disappeared in the H3 S10D hst2∆ smc2-8 triple mutant cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data showing genetic suppression.

claim: Enhanced activation of Hst2 (H3 S10D) suppressed the effect of the smc2-8 mutation on chromatin contraction.
source: Thus, enhanced activation of Hst2 (H3 S10D) suppressed the effect of the smc2-8 mutation on chromatin contraction.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data from double mutants.

claim: Hst2 might mediate the suppression of the contraction defect due to the smc2-8 mutation either through activation of a still unknown, alternative contraction pathway or through stimulation of condensin activity.
source: Hst2 might mediate the suppression of the contraction defect due to the smc2-8 mutation either through activation of a still unknown, alternative contraction pathway or through stimulation of condensin activity such as to restore at least part of its function.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the suppression data.

claim: The smc2-8 H3-S10A double mutant cells were growing slower than the smc2-8 single mutant cells.
source: Consistent with condensin and H3 S10 phosphorylation pathways acting synergistically to promote proper chromosome condensation, the smc2-8 H3-S10A double mutant cells were growing slower than the smc2-8 single mutant cells, and were unable to grow at 33°C, unlike the single mutant cells (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The smc2-8 H3-S10A double mutant cells were unable to grow at 33°C, unlike the single mutant cells.
source: Consistent with condensin and H3 S10 phosphorylation pathways acting synergistically to promote proper chromosome condensation, the smc2-8 H3-S10A double mutant cells were growing slower than the smc2-8 single mutant cells, and were unable to grow at 33°C, unlike the single mutant cells (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The smc2-8 hst2∆ double mutants showed the same phenotype as smc2-8 H3-S10A.
source: Accordingly, the smc2-8 hst2∆ double mutants showed the same phenotype.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: When the condensin complex was only partially active, cells depended on Hst2 and phosphorylation of histone H3 on S10 for growth.
source: Thus, when the condensin complex was only partially active, cells depended on Hst2 and phosphorylation of histone H3 on S10 for growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data showing synthetic growth defects.

claim: The smc2-8 H3 S10D double mutant did not show any altered or improved growth or viability phenotype compared with the smc2-8 single mutant cells.
source: Remarkably, however, the smc2-8 H3 S10D double mutant did not show any altered or improved growth or viability phenotype compared with the smc2-8 single mutant cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Restoring axial contraction of the chromosomes using the H3 S10D mutation was not sufficient to restore the viability of the cells lacking condensin function.
source: Thus, restoring axial contraction of the chromosomes using the H3 S10D mutation was not sufficient to restore the viability of the cells lacking condensin function.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data showing that H3 S10D does not suppress smc2-8 lethality.

claim: Condensin plays more roles than simply promoting the axial contraction of chromosomes.
source: These results are consistent with condensin playing more roles than simply promoting the axial contraction of chromosomes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that restoring contraction does not restore viability.

claim: At 25°C, the smc2-8 single and the smc2-8 H3 S10A, smc2-8 hst2∆ and smc2-8 H3 S10D double mutants cells showed no strong differences (6.3–8.0%) in the frequency at which lagging chromatin was observed in the center of the spindle.
source: At 25°C, the smc2-8 single and the smc2-8 H3 S10A, smc2-8 hst2∆ and smc2-8 H3 S10D double mutants cells showed no strong differences (6.3–8.0%) in the frequency at which lagging chromatin was observed in the center of the spindle (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The smc2-8 H3 S10A and the smc2-8 hst2∆ double mutants grown at 33°C showed a marked increase in the frequency (18.9% and 16.9%, respectively) of lagging chromatin compared with the smc2-8 single mutant cells.
source: In contrast, the smc2-8 H3 S10A and the smc2-8 hst2∆ double mutants grown at 33°C showed a marked increase in the frequency (18.9% and 16.9%, respectively) of lagging chromatin compared with the smc2-8 single mutant cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The smc2-8 H3 S10D mutant cells did not show an additive phenotype in lagging chromatin (10.0%).
source: The smc2-8 H3 S10D mutant cells did not show such an additive phenotype (10.0%; Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The pathways promoting the short-range compaction of chromatin and the axial contraction of chromosomes contribute synergistically to shaping mitotic chromosomes in order to ensure their correct segregation prior to cell division.
source: These data indicate that the pathways promoting the short-range compaction of chromatin and the axial contraction of chromosomes contribute synergistically to shaping mitotic chromosomes in order to ensure their correct segregation prior to cell division.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data showing synthetic defects in chromosome segregation.

claim: Mitotic chromosome condensation is the process through which a relatively relaxed interphase chromosome condenses into two relatively short, compact sister chromatids that the spindle can symmetrically segregate.
source: Mitotic chromosome condensation is the process through which a relatively relaxed interphase chromosome condenses into two relatively short, compact sister chromatids that the spindle can symmetrically segregate.
evidence: This is a definition based on established knowledge.

claim: The kinase aurora B has long been implicated in mitotic chromosome condensation.
source: The kinase aurora B has long been implicated in this process (Lavoie et al., 2004; Tada et al., 2011; Lavoie et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Aurora B is thought to promote the formation of a mitotic chromosome through activation of condensin and phosphorylation of S10 on histone H3.
source: Through activation of condensin and phosphorylation of S10 on histone H3 it is thought to promote the formation of a mitotic chromosome.
evidence: This is established knowledge about aurora B function.

claim: How these pathways interacted with each other to shape mitotic chromosomes was poorly understood.
source: However, how these pathways interacted with each other to shape mitotic chromosomes was poorly understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The fluorescence-based assay uses fluorophore quenching to show that nucleosome-nucleosome interaction via H3 phosphorylation and in an Hst2-dependent manner promotes short-range compaction of mitotic chromatin in vivo.
source: The second assay, introduced here, uses fluorophore quenching to show that nucleosome-nucleosome interaction via H3 phosphorylation and in an Hst2-dependent manner promotes short-range compaction of mitotic chromatin in vivo.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from the manuscript.

claim: The enhanced packing is evidenced by the increased quenching of fluorophores when the chromosome locus is decorated by multiple copies of a fluorescent reporter.
source: This enhanced packing is evidenced by the increased quenching of fluorophores when the chromosome locus is decorated by multiple copies of a fluorescent reporter.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from the manuscript.

claim: The quenching effect was observed similarly well whether GFP or mCherry was used as a fluorophore, and independently of whether it was fused to TetR or to LacI.
source: The quenching effect was observed similarly well whether we used GFP or mCherry as a fluorophore, and independently of whether it was fused to TetR or to LacI.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from multiple reporter systems.

claim: Chromatin compaction does not displace DNA-associated proteins such as TetR or LacI, as a strong cleansing model would predict.
source: Our studies establish that chromatin compaction does not displace DNA-associated proteins such as TetR or LacI, as a strong cleansing model would predict.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data showing that co-expression of TetR-GFP and TetR-mCherry prevents quenching.

claim: Compaction might serve functions such as to change the biophysical properties of the chromatin fiber during segregation.
source: Although they do not exclude that other DNA-binding factors might be removed from the DNA during this process, these data suggest that compaction might serve other functions, such as to change the biophysical properties of the chromatin fiber during segregation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: Chromatin compaction might affect the local stiffness, elasticity and mechanical resistance of chromosomes to facilitate their decatenation, protection and movement during anaphase.
source: Chromatin compaction might for example affect the local stiffness, elasticity and mechanical resistance of chromosomes to facilitate their decatenation, protection and movement during anaphase.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the function of chromatin compaction.

claim: The H3 S10D mutation is able to establish an Hst2-dependent and constitutive state of compaction and contraction.
source: Related to this, it is remarkable that the H3 S10D mutation is able to establish an Hst2-dependent and constitutive state of compaction and contraction, as evidenced by both assays, without affecting much growth and viability.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from H3 S10D mutants.

claim: H3 S10D might lead to hyper-activation of chromatin compaction by over-recruitment of Hst2, such that it might shorten the chromosome axis, independently of the contraction machinery.
source: In the first, H3 S10D might lead to hyper-activation of chromatin compaction by over-recruitment of Hst2, such that it might shorten the chromosome axis, independently of the contraction machinery.
evidence: This is a speculative model to explain H3 S10D effects.

claim: Crosslinking studies do not indicate that H3 S10D increases nucleosome-nucleosome interaction.
source: However, the following observations speak against this idea: I. crosslinking studies do not indicate that H3 S10D increases nucleosome-nucleosome interaction (Wilkins et al., 2014), II. fluorescence quenching of TetR-mCherry and LacI-GFP is not enhanced in the H3 S10D mutant (Figure 1B,C) compared with WT anaphase cells, and III. phosphorylation of H3 S10 does promote the condensin-dependent and Hst2-dependent contraction of artificially long chromosomes (Neurohr et al., 2011; Wilkins et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Fluorescence quenching of TetR-mCherry and LacI-GFP is not enhanced in the H3 S10D mutant compared with WT anaphase cells.
source: However, the following observations speak against this idea: I. crosslinking studies do not indicate that H3 S10D increases nucleosome-nucleosome interaction (Wilkins et al., 2014), II. fluorescence quenching of TetR-mCherry and LacI-GFP is not enhanced in the H3 S10D mutant (Figure 1B,C) compared with WT anaphase cells, and III. phosphorylation of H3 S10 does promote the condensin-dependent and Hst2-dependent contraction of artificially long chromosomes (Neurohr et al., 2011; Wilkins et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: Phosphorylation of H3 S10 does promote the condensin-dependent and Hst2-dependent contraction of artificially long chromosomes.
source: However, the following observations speak against this idea: I. crosslinking studies do not indicate that H3 S10D increases nucleosome-nucleosome interaction (Wilkins et al., 2014), II. fluorescence quenching of TetR-mCherry and LacI-GFP is not enhanced in the H3 S10D mutant (Figure 1B,C) compared with WT anaphase cells, and III. phosphorylation of H3 S10 does promote the condensin-dependent and Hst2-dependent contraction of artificially long chromosomes (Neurohr et al., 2011; Wilkins et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Hst2 may stimulate condensin function, and hyper-activation of Hst2 by H3 S10D may promote this effect and thereby chromosome arm contraction.
source: Thus, these data support an alternative model: Hst2 may stimulate condensin function, and hyper-activation of Hst2 by H3 S10D may promote this effect and thereby chromosome arm contraction.
evidence: This is a speculative model based on experimental observations.

claim: The phenotype of the H3 S10D mutant cells does not seem to reflect physiological conditions taking place during regular mitoses.
source: Furthermore, it is important to note that the phenotype of the H3 S10D mutant cells does not seem to reflect physiological conditions taking place during regular mitoses, indicating that the fraction of Hst2 driving wild type chromosome contraction does not depend on H3 S10 phosphorylation (dashed arrow Figure 7, left panel).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the observation that H3 S10A does not affect regular mitosis.

claim: The H3 S10D phenotype might reflect what happens when both chromosome condensation pathways are hyper-activated, for example under the presence of an artificially long chromosome or in small cells.
source: Rather, it might reflect what happens when both chromosome condensation pathways are hyper-activated, for example under the presence of an artificially long chromosome or in small cells, such as cells grown on a poor carbon source (see below).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the H3 S10D phenotype.

claim: The H3 S10D strain does not show any obvious defects in growth and viability despite causing chromatin compaction and contraction throughout the cell cycle.
source: In any case, it is striking that the H3 S10D strain does not show any obvious defects in growth and viability despite causing chromatin compaction and contraction throughout the cell cycle.
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations of H3 S10D growth.

claim: The constitutively condensed state in H3 S10D does not impair access and remodeling of chromatin by the transcription and replication machineries during interphase in any major manner.
source: Thus, this constitutively condensed state does not impair access and remodeling of chromatin by the transcription and replication machineries during interphase in any major manner.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that H3 S10D cells grow normally.

claim: Chromatin undergoes a number of successive structural changes during anaphase and compaction precedes contraction.
source: Our kinetic data suggest that chromatin undergoes a number of successive structural changes during anaphase and that compaction precedes contraction.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on kinetic data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Residual cohesion between sister chromatids persists during early anaphase and this actually causes chromosome stretching during early segregation stages.
source: However, previous work has established that residual cohesion between sister chromatids persists during early anaphase and that this actually causes chromosome stretching during early segregation stages (Renshaw et al., 2010; Harrison et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Maximum contraction is only reached when cohesion is fully resolved, such as to not interfere with cohesion removal.
source: Thus, a second model would be that maximum contraction is only reached when cohesion is fully resolved, such as to not interfere with cohesion removal.
evidence: This is a speculative model to explain the timing of contraction.

claim: Chromosome contraction needs to be a late anaphase event to complete chromosome segregation.
source: This scenario suggests that chromosome contraction indeed needs to be a late anaphase event to complete chromosome segregation, and that perhaps the compaction events that precede play an important role in facilitating cohesion resolution.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the timing of contraction.

claim: Compaction events that precede contraction might play an important role in facilitating cohesion resolution.
source: This scenario suggests that chromosome contraction indeed needs to be a late anaphase event to complete chromosome segregation, and that perhaps the compaction events that precede play an important role in facilitating cohesion resolution.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the function of early compaction.

claim: Arm contraction and chromatin compaction undergo relaxation between late anaphase and G1.
source: However, one definite conclusion that we can already draw is that arm contraction and chromatin compaction undergo relaxation between late anaphase and G1, since these nuclei are not significantly different in size, and hence the effects observed are not due to confinement alone.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data showing similar nuclear sizes but different compaction states.

claim: Mitotic chromosome condensation entails at least three processes.
source: Based on our data on chromosome contraction and compaction in Figure 3C, we propose that mitotic chromosome condensation entails at least three processes (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A histone 3-dependent and histone 4-dependent process ensures the short-range tightening of DNA into a smaller volume via nucleosome-nucleosome interaction.
source: First, a histone 3-dependent and histone 4-dependent process, which we term chromatin compaction, ensures the short-range tightening of DNA into a smaller volume via nucleosome-nucleosome interaction (Wilkins et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data and supported by a citation.

claim: Chromatin compaction strictly depends on the phosphorylation of histone H3 on serine 10, and the subsequent deacetylation of lysine 16 of histone H4.
source: This process strictly depends on the phosphorylation of histone H3 on serine 10, and the subsequent deacetylation of lysine 16 of histone H4.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from histone mutants.

claim: Chromatin compaction has little impact on the length of condensed chromosomes.
source: Because this event has little impact on the length of condensed chromosomes, it has escaped attention until now.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the observation that H3 S10A does not affect chromosome length.

claim: Chromatin compaction is an important event for proper chromosome architecture and is an early event of every yeast mitosis.
source: However, our data indicate that it is an important event for proper chromosome architecture and is an early event of every yeast mitosis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data showing timing and importance of compaction.

claim: A condensin-dependent process ensures the long-range contraction of the chromosome, probably by facilitating the formation of higher order chromatin structures along the chromosome axis.
source: Second, a condensin-dependent process, termed here axial chromosome contraction, ensures the long-range contraction of the chromosome, probably by facilitating the formation of higher order chromatin structures along the chromosome axis (Cuylen and Haering, 2011; Baxter and Aragón, 2012).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data and supported by citations.

claim: Axial chromosome contraction is completed after chromatin compaction, in late anaphase, but does not strictly require it in order to proceed.
source: This process is completed after chromatin compaction, in late anaphase, but does not strictly require it in order to proceed.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data showing independent pathways.

claim: Hst2 contributes to both compaction and contraction processes.
source: Certainly, it will be interesting to clarify this order of event, to dissect how it is controlled, and to determine whether it facilitates the ordered condensation of well-separated chromosome arms. Moreover, the observation that Hst2 contributes to both processes suggests that this enzyme might be pivotal for coordinating compaction and contraction with each other.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data showing effects of hst2Δ on both processes.

claim: Hst2 might be pivotal for coordinating compaction and contraction with each other.
source: Certainly, it will be interesting to clarify this order of event, to dissect how it is controlled, and to determine whether it facilitates the ordered condensation of well-separated chromosome arms. Moreover, the observation that Hst2 contributes to both processes suggests that this enzyme might be pivotal for coordinating compaction and contraction with each other.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on Hst2's role in both processes.

claim: There exists an additional, also condensin-dependent process devoted to some other aspect of chromosome organization, beyond compaction and contraction.
source: Third, our data also indicate the existence of an additional, also condensin-dependent process devoted to some other aspect of chromosome organization, beyond compaction and contraction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that restoring contraction does not restore viability.

claim: Restoring the contraction of the chromosome along its axis in the smc2-8 condensin mutant cells by mimicking constitutive H3 phosphorylation did not alleviate the temperature-dependent lethality caused by the smc2-8 mutation.
source: Indeed, restoring the contraction of the chromosome along its axis in the smc2-8 condensin mutant cells by mimicking constitutive H3 phosphorylation did not alleviate the temperature-dependent lethality caused by the smc2-8 mutation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Although inactivation of the deacetylase Hst2 largely abolished the axial contraction of chromosomes, HST2 is not an essential gene.
source: Furthermore, although inactivation of the deacetylase Hst2 largely abolished the axial contraction of chromosomes, HST2 is not an essential gene.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and the fact that hst2Δ cells are viable.

claim: The essential function of condensin is not to mediate long-range contraction.
source: Hence, we suggest that the essential function of condensin is not to mediate long-range contraction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that HST2 is not essential despite affecting contraction.

claim: The essential function of condensin most likely relates to its roles in orchestrating the decatenation of intertwined sister-chromatids and the re-annealing of single stranded DNAs.
source: Rather, the essential function of condensin most likely relates to its roles in orchestrating the decatenation of intertwined sister-chromatids (Charbin et al., 2014; Baxter and Aragón, 2012; Baxter et al., 2011) and the re-annealing of single stranded DNAs (Sakai et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Yeast cells challenged by the presence of an exceptionally long chromosome or by being themselves exceptionally small possess the ability to condense chromosomes beyond wild type levels to adjust the axial contraction of long chromosomes and adapt their length to the length of the spindle.
source: In an earlier study we demonstrated that yeast cells challenged by the presence of an exceptionally long chromosome or by being themselves exceptionally small (for example, whi3 mutant cells and cells growing on a poor carbon source) possess the ability to condense chromosomes beyond wild type levels to adjust the axial contraction of long chromosomes and adapt their length to the length of the spindle, a process we termed adaptive hyper-condensation (Neurohr et al., 2011), and which we would like to rename adaptive hyper-contraction.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Adaptive hyper-contraction depended on condensin and phosphorylation of H3 S10.
source: This process depended on condensin and phosphorylation of H3 S10, this last requirement being in contrast to what is observed for the contraction of most wild type chromosomes during regular mitoses.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Single smc2-8 and H3 S10A mutants failed to hyper-contract an exceptionally long chromosome.
source: Accordingly, single smc2-8 and H3 S10A mutants failed to hyper-contract an exceptionally long chromosome (Neurohr et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Adaptive hyper-contraction depended more heavily on Ipl1-dependent phosphorylation of S10 on histone H3 than regular chromosome condensation does.
source: Since the H3 S10A mutation had no defect on the axial contraction of wild type chromosomes, these results indicated that adaptive hyper-contraction depended more heavily on Ipl1-dependent phosphorylation of S10 on histone H3 than regular chromosome condensation does.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential requirement for H3 S10 in different contexts.

claim: H3 S10 is hyper-phosphorylated on long chromosomes by Ipl1 located in the center of the spindle (midzone), boosting Hst2 and condensin activity.
source: Thus, we propose that H3 S10 is hyper-phosphorylated on long chromosomes by Ipl1 located in the center of the spindle (midzone), boosting Hst2 and condensin activity (dotted arrow, Figure 7).
evidence: This is a speculative model to explain adaptive hyper-contraction.

claim: Mimicking S10 phosphorylation, using the H3 S10D allele, promotes axial shortening in an Hst2-dependent manner.
source: Our observation that mimicking S10 phosphorylation, using the H3 S10D allele, promotes axial shortening in an Hst2-dependent manner is indeed consistent with high levels of S10 phosphorylation promoting the crosstalk between compaction and contraction, via Hst2.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from H3 S10D mutants.

claim: High levels of S10 phosphorylation promote the crosstalk between compaction and contraction, via Hst2.
source: Our observation that mimicking S10 phosphorylation, using the H3 S10D allele, promotes axial shortening in an Hst2-dependent manner is indeed consistent with high levels of S10 phosphorylation promoting the crosstalk between compaction and contraction, via Hst2.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from H3 S10D mutants.

claim: Yeast is a powerful system to dissect the mechanisms underlying chromosome condensation and how the disruption of such mechanisms affects chromosome segregation and cell viability.
source: Together, our work demonstrates that yeast is a powerful system to dissect the mechanisms underlying chromosome condensation and how the disruption of such mechanisms affects chromosome segregation and cell viability.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the findings presented in the manuscript.
